title: You didn’t just drift… you chose distance.
paragraphs: You didn’t just drift… you chose distance.
That quiet panic when you realize—God feels far… and you don’t know how to get back.
But here’s the question you’ve been avoiding:
What if He’s not the one who moved?

What if every ignored conviction…
every delayed obedience…
every “I’ll fix it later”…
Was a step away from Him?
And now you’re standing in a place you never planned to be.
Some of you didn’t wake up one day and decide to rebel.

Tired of fighting sin.
Tired of waiting on God.
Tired of being “different.”

Until the thing you once resisted…
became the thing you now hide.
Thriving in private while you smile in public.
You know you’re not where you used to be.
You know your fire isn’t burning the same.
You know your heart has grown… quieter.
You’ve started to get used to it.
“Return to me, declares the LORD Almighty, and I will return to you.” — Zechariah 1:3
Not that God’s grace runs out—
“Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.” — Hebrews 3:15
Because every delay… shapes your heart.
Some scholars interpret this hardening as a gradual numbing—where repeated resistance to God’s voice makes repentance feel harder over time.
And maybe that’s where you are right now.

You don’t cry like you used to.
You don’t pray like you used to.
You don’t feel like you used to.
The fear you feel right now?
And this is where the story shifts.
Because Christianity is not about managing your behavior.
It’s about returning to a Person.
Jesus didn’t come for the cleaned-up version of you.
He came for the version of you that’s hiding.
The one kneeling in the dirt.
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
While you were still in it.
And it did not disqualify you.
But here’s the truth most people avoid:
Grace is free—but it’s not casual.
Jesus didn’t die so you could stay stuck.
He died so you could be free.
Which means returning to God is not just emotional.

Turning your mind.
Turning your direction.
Turning your allegiance.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
And here’s the picture you need to see—
The Father is not standing with crossed arms.
“But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion for him; he ran to his son…” — Luke 15:20
He didn’t wait at the door.
That means the moment you turn—
So let me ask you, not as a preacher…
But as someone who cares about your soul:
What are you still holding onto that’s keeping you from coming home?
Is it really worth the distance?
Is it really worth the silence?
Is it really worth losing intimacy with God?
And God is not exposing this to shame you.
He’s exposing it to save you.
Come back to the One who never stopped loving you.
You don’t need a perfect prayer.

“Lord… I’ve drifted.
But I’m coming back.”
You might be the interruption they need.
But don’t wait until your heart forgets how to return.
“We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.”
